I remember the first time I accidentally locked my keys in my car. It was a Friday afternoon, and I was in a rush to pick up groceries before heading to a friend's house for dinner. I had a keychain with several keys, but I'm not the most organized person. As I was unlocking the car, I must have absentmindedly put the wrong key into the lock. Panic set in as the key wouldn't fit, and I tried to unlock the door with all the other keys, to no avail. My heart was racing; my hands were shaking. I tried everything I could think of, but it was no use. I was locked in.

With no other options, I grabbed my phone and called a locksmith. While I was waiting for them to arrive, I sat in my car and tried to calm down. I took deep breaths and listened to the sound of my own heartbeat. It was a strange and somewhat surreal experience. I realized that in my haste, I had forgotten the simple, yet crucial step of double-checking which key I was using.
